properties.statement: "WHICH OF MY RULES HAVE NO DETECTOR?" IS NOT A QUESTION THE GRAPH CAN BE ASKED — AND REFLOW2'S OWN ANSWER IS FOUR OUT OF FOUR. Proposed by dev_storyflow's api-boss 5d608b85, 2026-08-08, as the one high-leverage item in a GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN opportunity built on Anthony's own words. MEASURED HERE THE SAME DAY, and the number is the argument: reflow2 has 5 DesignRules; FOUR carry `enforced: true` (rule:bl-135, rule:bl-212, rule:bl-41, rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party) which the schema defines as 'violations are gate-blocking'; and NOT ONE of the five has an incoming VERIFIES edge. Four rules that block the build, zero detectors, and no report names it. THE MECHANISM: `schema/verify.yaml:80` declares VERIFIES as `from: Verification, to: "*"`. The wildcard ACCEPTS a DesignRule target — nothing is broken — but it does not MODEL it, so `describe_schema` ranks it as merely accepted and no detector treats rules as verifiable things. AGENTS.md already warns about exactly this distinction: 'several will validate, and validating is not the same as meaning what you intended.' Here the cost of the wildcard is not a wrong edge but an unaskable question. THEIR EVIDENCE, which is stronger than ours: in ONE session that fleet found five rules with no check — a routing rule naming a file that names no worker entry point; a verification step that false-negatives on a shared tree; a comms rule whose quoted example is a forgeable handshake; a claim protocol with no detector for its own bypass; and a detector built for that bypass that was blind to it. Their words: 'Every one is a RULE WITHOUT A CHECK, and no report could have listed them, because the graph cannot currently be asked.' FIX SHAPE, theirs, and it is small: enumerate VERIFIES' `to:` explicitly rather than leaving it wildcard, then make `enforced: true` with no incoming VERIFIES a detectable defect. CHECKED BEFORE PROPOSING, twice. (1) THE STAMP DOES NOT MOVE: it carries `edge_type_names`, `edge_types`, `node_type_names`, `node_types`, `schema_version` — not endpoint lists — so modelling the endpoints owes NO upgrade doc, which makes this far cheaper than a normal schema change. (2) THE SAFE ENUMERATION IS KNOWN: VERIFIES today points at Capability (126), Requirement (3), Artifact (3), Component (1), so narrowing must include all four or it would invalidate live edges. THEIR COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS THE BEST PART AND MUST SURVIVE INTO THE BUILD: 'A GRAPH NODE GREEN-WASHES EXACTLY LIKE A DOCUMENT' — proven twice in their own graph, where nine directory artifacts swallowed 373 files while the check read green. Governance-in-graph without executable checks is prettier prose with identical blind spots, which is why the DETECTOR is the proposal and the vocabulary is not.
